messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for redwood-runtime-prod: high-kv-cache-growth (severity=high) — pager: @oncall-rotation, runbook: <https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache|kv-cache runbook>

alex.k: paging in — seeing huge KV cache size on qwen-mqa-13b pods in us-west-2, memory OOMs starting at ~15:03 UTC. p99 latency spiking > 4s for text-generation routes.

maya.p: confirmed in metrics — continuous batching rate jumped ~6x around 15:00, kv entries exploded. I see sequence length distribution skewed by a customer workload with many short prompts but weirdly long prefix reuse.

dan.r: any recent rollout? config changes?

alex.k: no deploys to runtime in last 2 hours. We rolled a model config change for a canary yesterday but that was in eu-central.

priya.s: attaching logs snippet:
```
[15:02:31] runtime: batcher=continuous batch_size=2048 seq_len=1024 kv_cache_entries=1.2M mem_used=45GB
[15:02:45] runtime: batcher=continuous batch_size=4096 seq_len=512 kv_cache_entries=2.8M mem_used=92GB
[15:03:10] model=qwen-mqa-13b shard=3 oom while allocating KV cache
```

sandeep: looks like MQA-specific path blowing up kv sizing when certain prompts trigger cross-sequence caching. Known edge case?

maya.p: there was a recent model-variant calibration for qwen-mqa to enable longer kv retention (ttl=600s). That would increase steady-state size.

alex.k: impact: several paying customers on dedicated pools (us-west-2) are seeing 50-100% latency regressions and some failures. Need immediate mitigation — prefer config hotfix before full rollout revert.

priya.s: mitigation options:
- disable continuous batching on affected pool(s)
- reduce batch_size and limit seq_len ceiling (e.g., seq_len_max=256)
- reduce KV TTL / enable aggressive pruning
- fallback routing to a non-MQA-compatible model variant (mistral-7b) for impacted customers

dan.r: can we flip continuous batching off for us-west qwen-mqa pool without restart? There's a dynamic flag in runtime: `runtime.flags.continuous_batching=false`

maya.p: yes we can, it's dynamic. I'll push flag to false for the us-west pool and lower max_batch to 512. Also set `kv_cache.ttl=30s` temporarily.

alex.k: do it. Put commands/snippet you will run in thread so we have audit.

maya.p: running now:
```bash
# Toggle continuous batching and reduce batch size on us-west-2 qwen-mqa pool
redwoodctl runtime set-flag --pool us-west-2-qwen-mqa --flag continuous_batching=false
redwoodctl runtime update-pool --pool us-west-2-qwen-mqa --max_batch_size 512 --seq_len_max 256
redwoodctl runtime set-config --pool us-west-2-qwen-mqa --kv-ttl 30s
```

(3 minutes later)
maya.p: applied. Monitoring...

priya.s: metrics: kv entries dropping from 2.8M -> 300k over 90s, mem_used down from 92GB -> 28GB, p99 latency back to ~650ms.

alex.k: good. Open question: root cause — ttl change + continuous batching exposing an MQA kv-sizing bug? We should capture heap/kv state and create a proper incident ticket.

sandeep: agree, likely MQA path miscalculates key dedup across interleaved batches. I'll instrument a repro on a canary with a crafted prompt set.

dan.r: customers impacted list? Emily, can support help triage customers on the thread? @emily_support_bot

emily_support_bot: I pulled active sessions flagged in the window 15:00-15:10 UTC. Affected customers: acme-ai (dedicated), healthlytics (dedicated), three trial orgs. I've opened support cases and notified AMs.

alex.k: next steps:
- short-term: keep continuous_batching=false and kv_ttl=30s for us-west until patch (owner: maya)
- immediate: route new requests for identified customers to mistral-7b fallback where acceptable (owner: dan)
- medium: SRE+ML to reproduce and root cause (owner: sandeep + dan)
- postmortem + runbook update for MQA kv sizing (owner: alex)

maya.p: I'll schedule a controlled rollback to enable batching on a single canary node once sandeep has added extra logging. For now setting autoscaler to keep more headroom.

priya.s: I'll send a short customer impact note to status page draft: "Intermittent generation failures and increased latency for customers using Qwen-MQA in us-west-2. Mitigation applied, engineering investigating."

alex.k: handing over to night oncall — maya, can you take the 4-hour follow-up? I'll be off at 18:00 UTC.

maya.p: taking handoff. Leaving notes: keep continuous_batching off for pool, monitor p99 and kv entries, escalate to sandeep if kv grows > 750k.

oncall-rotation: handover recorded. Next oncall: @dan.r at 19:00 UTC.

dan.r: thanks. I'll follow up on repro + put together a test harness that simulates MQA interleaved prefixes. Will also look for a quick code patch to bound kv growth when retention policy miscalculates.

alex.k: summary for incident ticket:
- alert: high-kv-cache-growth on qwen-mqa in us-west-2 (1771203456)
- mitigation: disabled continuous batching, reduced max_batch_size, set kv_ttl to 30s, routed some customers to fallback models
- impact: increased latency and failures for multiple dedicated customers; resolved by mitigation for now
- owners: maya (mitigation), sandeep (root cause), dan (repro/patch), alex (postmortem)

priya.s: filing the incident in PagerDuty/Incident tracker with timeline and impact. I'll add customers contacted.

(almost 2 hours later)
sandeep: repro done on canary — MQA key-combine logic double-counts keys when continuous batching merges partial sequences; creating PR to clamp kv growth + unit tests. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4827

alex.k: excellent. Plan to roll fix to canary and then us-west after validation. Keep this thread updated.

maya.p: canary with patch shows stable kv entries under similar workload. I'll schedule a staged roll to us-west in 30m, and then to global if green.

emily_support_bot: customer update sent: "We applied a mitigation that restored latency and reduced errors. Engineering is rolling a permanent fix; we will follow up with a detailed postmortem." :white_check_mark:

(end)
